title: ‘Drawing a line in the sand’: Democrats put Trump admin on notice over alleged document destruction | CNN Politics
text:
Source: CNN

Democrats and the White House are already in a showdown over alleged document destruction — and the party hasn’t even taken control of Congress yet.

Democratic lawmakers and investigators are increasingly concerned that the Trump administration is destroying documents and not adhering to preservation record laws before they take control of Congress, setting off a flurry of letters across the federal government demanding officials properly save documents and turn off auto-delete settings on encrypted messaging applications.

The White House has said that Democrats are making claims over document destruction by the administration without evidence, but has also indicated it sees no obligation to comply with their demands to preserve or turn over documents before they gain control of committee gavels in January.

The high-stakes standoff is laying the groundwork for a legal fight, as Democrats prepare for far-reaching investigations into the Trump administration and fear that document destruction could hinder their ability to conduct oversight.

“What I think you’re seeing in Congress with these document preservation letters is Congress is drawing a line in the sand and maintaining a record so that if people do destroy records they could potentially be prosecuted in a future administration for obstruction of Congress,” Jim Secreto, who worked in the Obama White House Counsel’s office on congressional investigations and compliance with the Presidential Records Act, told CNN.

Democratic Rep. Jamie Raskin, who is in line to chair the House Judiciary Committee, is particularly concerned about the use of Signal by federal employees as a way to circumvent future Democratic oversight.

In a series of preservation letters sent to the Department of Justice, Federal Bureau of Investigation, Department of Homeland Security, Immigration and Customs Enforcement and the Bureau of Prisons, Raskin raised concerns about the potential for document destruction.

A White House official told CNN, “we comply with all federal record retention laws and regulations.”

CNN has reached out to the Justice Department and the Department of Homeland Security to request comment.

“There is significant evidence that Trump Administration officials have engaged in the widespread destruction, mutilation, and concealment of government records, seemingly with the express purpose of circumventing federal record preservation laws. This attempt to evade transparency extends to the highest levels of federal agencies, including top-ranking law enforcement officials,” Raskin said in the letters.

In the letters, Raskin said that a Signal conversation between the general counsel of the FBI and an associate of Donald Trump Jr. appeared to have been set for messages to auto-delete after a week. The Democratic lawmaker said that the conversation concerned “a potential or ongoing investigation involving an individual wanted by federal authorities on health care fraud and related charges.”

“This incident, just one of many that have already been reported to our Committee, raises significant concerns that DOJ and FBI officials are openly flouting federal law when it comes to the preservation of official government records,” Raskin said.

Judiciary Committee staffers plan to rely on whistleblowers and third parties to help them get the information they seek, but are hoping that the preservation letters sent Friday will put a stop to the use of Signal and auto-delete settings for official work by federal employees.

“We want them to be on notice that this behavior is wrong. And if they are doing it, and especially if they continue doing it, we will draw inferences from your destruction of evidence. That’s something that every litigate is familiar with, both in the civil and criminal context,” a Democratic source familiar told CNN.

White House Counsel Will Scharf sent letters earlier this week to Democratic committee leaderssayingthe Trump administration’s position is that no official has to comply with their demands to preserve or turn over documents and information because Democrats do not yet chair the committees, according to a copy of the letter obtained by CNN.

On Thursday, Raskin received a preservation letter of his own from US Attorney Aaron Reitz, who accused the Maryland Democrat of weaponizing his investigative efforts without a legislative purpose to go after Trump associates and the administration.

Scharf wrote that the purpose of the letters sent by Democrats “is not legitimate oversight but to harass and aggrandize.”

“In the days since the November 3, 2026 election, several Ranking Members have sent letters to the Executive Branch demanding documents or information. Some of these letters imply, without evidence, that thousands of United States government employees are conspiring to destroy documents in violation of the Federal Records Act,” he said.

In addition to calling on agencies to preserve their documents, Raskin is demanding Attorney General Todd Blanche and other Trump officials open an inquiry into what documents may have been deleted and attempt to recover those records.

Even though Democrats don’t yet have the authority to compel document production with subpoena power, these preservation letters serve as a preview of what’s to come, particularly if Democrats regain control of the White House in 2028.

“It’s the type of thing that a future Department of Justice could use as evidence in court of intent to destroy records,” Secreto told CNN.
